note: What a snippet has to contain to be worth publishing, and how much of the corpus is allowed to fail that today. harness/snippets.py locates every endpoint in every target and the coverage gate is green, but a located snippet is not a captured one: 403 of them are a bare annotation and several hundred more are a registration naming a handler that lives somewhere else. Those are counted here rather than gated red, because a gate that went red on them would block every branch that is fixing them. An allowance only ever goes down: harness/snippets.py --ratchet rewrites this file from what the tree actually does, and --check fails on anything above it.

not_only_annotations.label: annotation-only
not_only_annotations.what: a snippet may not be nothing but annotations, attributes and comments
not_only_annotations.why: @Get("/json/small") names the route, passes both coverage checks, and says nothing about what answers the request

reaches_domain.label: not reaching the domain
reaches_domain.what: a handler and its support together must name something the shared domain gave the file
reaches_domain.why: a registration that names a handler defined elsewhere is complete, correct, and shows a reader nothing. The shared domain is where the behaviour is, so a snippet that never gets there has not captured the endpoint
